title: Barney Carnage 2.0
decision: Motion gate sufficient for bounded diagnostic comparison; proceed with six total captures, three at 25 MHz and three at 12 MHz, alternating.
gate_observation: Both images show the same white playfield, menu bar and two zero counters. The colored target is near the upper right in A and lower/left in B. Visible displacement establishes active motion between screenshots.
timing_limit: These are gate timestamps spanning screenshot/tool gaps, not exact image acquisition timestamps or a 10-second movement benchmark. No velocity inferred.
phase_requirement: Match active white-field/no-shot starting state, displayed counters and fresh-load input/settling procedure; record target position/phase per repetition rather than requiring identical coordinates.
level_limit: Level 1 label/story not visible in these screenshots and not observed separately in this fresh gate. Describe the scene by observed readiness rather than asserting Level 1.
controls: Fresh reload per repetition, same single centered start click and settling interval where reproducible; visible/focused; same bundle/browser/render settings; confirm actual cpuMhz. Record starting/ending target positions and counters outside timing.
stop_rule: Stop if fresh reload cannot reproduce the white active field, counters differ unexpectedly, scene transitions or target is no longer demonstrably active; document invalid captures and do not silently compare different scenes. Random/different target phase alone is not a blocker.
interpretation: Compare clock/work/backlog medians and ranges only as a bounded scene diagnostic. Target phase can change workload and must be acknowledged. No original pace, scoring, full gameplay or fidelity qualification follows.
